 Order

The petitioners have sought to challenge the order passed in Misc.No.10016/2014 (LAC) dated 27.08.2016 by the learned IV Additional District and Sessions Judge at Doddaballapura, raising various grounds including that the petitioners have right in the property that was acquired and they were not arrayed as parties in Misc.No.10016/2014.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Learned counsel appearing for respondent No.4 submits that the impugned order in Misc.No.10016/2014 being passed on the basis of the petition filed under Section 3H(4) of the National Highways Act, 1956 (hereinafter referred to as 'the NH Act' for short) at the instance of the Special Land Acquisition Officer and the Competent Authority and after adjudication, an order being passed, the appropriate remedy as against such order would be to file first appeal by construing the order passed in Misc.No.10016/2014 as an adjudication and the learned counsel relies on the judgment in the case of Smt.Gowramma Vs. The Spl. Land Acquisition Officer and Others1.
ILR 2010 KAR 4186 3.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that the present case is not technically a reference as understood insofar as the petition filed by the Highways Authorities itself.

4. Heard both sides insofar as the preliminary objection regarding maintainability as raised by learned counsel appearing for respondent No.4.
5.
It is noticed that a petition was filed under Section 3H(4) of the NH Act before the District and Sessions Judge, Bangalore Rural District.

entities.text: District and Sessions Judge, Bangalore Rural District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The petition was filed as a reference petition as there was inter-se dispute between the parties.
Section 3H(4) of the NH Act provides for mechanism for reference of the dispute to the decision of the Competent Court and accordingly, reference was sought for.

It is clear that once an amount is determined and in the event, several persons claimed to be interested, the Competent Authority may under Section 3H(4) of the NH Act, refer the dispute before the Competent Court.
In the present case, the reference petition details the dispute at para No.7 of the reference petition and accordingly, reference was made.
The final order passed in the miscellaneous petition results in adjudication of rights and entitlements.

If that were to be so,
adjudication of rights in the miscellaneous petition and the order passed would lead to construing the order falling within the expression decree under Section 2(2) of CPC as noticed by the Sri N S Nagaraju vs Sri Krishnappa on 2 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140512489/

sentences.text:
Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in Gowramma's case (supra).
8.
Taking note of the law laid down in Gowramma's case (supra), the present petition is not maintainable.
The substantive remedy is an appeal.
9. Accordingly, petition is rejected.
Liberty is reserved to the petitioners to workout the substantive remedy against the order passed in Misc.No.10016/2014.

Needless to state, in light of prosecution of proceedings before this forum, which it is submitted was due to bona-fide mistake, the time spent before this Court is to be excluded while taking note of the aspect of limitation in challenging the impugned order.
Needless to state, in the event of any further compensation becoming due, the procedure under Section 3H(4) of the NH Act will have to be followed including the petitioners herein.
All contentions are left open.
Office to return the certified copy of the order.

It is further clarified that, the benefit of the order as regards exclusion of time in the appeal as observed would enure to the benefit of the petitioners, if steps are taken to challenge the impugned order in miscellaneous petition within a period of three weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of the order.

Insofar as apprehension of the petitioners that the order in miscellaneous petition may be made use of henceforth prejudicing the petitioners, the interim order passed in W.P.No.16085/2017, granting stay of the order passed in miscellaneous petition would be extended for a period of four weeks.

In light of the submission made and taking note of the order passed on 18.04.2017 in W.P.No.16085/2017, there would be interim order staying the order in miscellaneous petition for a period of four weeks.
Accordingly, petition is disposed off.
